lines.trans: I will eat at work today.
Livelier, livelier, let's work!
Come on, wake up faster.
A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?
We are frying, frying our bacon.
Wake up everyone, morning has already arrived.
What did you lose in my kitchen?
I am doing your job for you.
Who is this secret guest?
It is a method of inspection in a hotel.
The inspector stays here like an ordinary guest.
He inspects the work of all hotel departments.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: moving or capable of moving at high speed

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

examples.text: Большое спасибо за вашу быструю помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your quick help!

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to fry', forming an aspectual pair with 'пожарить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Повар жарит сочное мясо на сковороде.
examples.trans: The cook fries juicy meat on the pan.

examples.text: Нет, Федя сам жарил эту куропатку!
examples.trans: No, Fedya roasted that partridge himself!

examples.text: Я просто жарю рыбу на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: I simply fry fish on a hot pan.

meanings.note: comparative adverb used as imperative spur

examples.trans: Come on, come on, faster, guys!
Move lively, sluggards, let us begin working together!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
Fitting the highest standard. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ideal, perfect').

examples.text: Мы создадим идеальную команду для работы.
examples.trans: We will create an ideal team for work.

examples.text: Сегодня стояла идеальная погода для прогулки.
examples.trans: Today there was ideal weather for a walk.
For ideal order in the universe.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

наступить.gloss: to come (of time); to step on

meanings.en: to come, to set in (night, winter, a moment)
meanings.note: Наступила ночь = night has fallen. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come (of time); to step on', paired with 'наступать'.

Наступить на + accusative. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come (of time); to step on', paired with 'наступать'.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.
Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это гематома, она и стала причиной потери памяти.
examples.trans: That is a hematoma, it became the cause of memory loss.

examples.text: Андрей, положи её к себе, а то и эту потеряю.
examples.trans: Andrey, put it in your pocket, or I will lose this one too.

examples.text: Я хотел бы просмотреть все документы по закупке продуктов.
examples.trans: I would like to review all the documents on food purchases.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'быстрее').

examples.trans: A bit faster, well, where is our bacon?

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно побыстрее и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite a bit faster and calmly.

поесть.gloss: to eat, to have a meal

meanings.en: to eat, to have something to eat
meanings.note: Perfective of есть. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat, to have a meal', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Ну ладно, брось! Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: Oh come on, stop it! We'll only eat.

meanings.note: по порядку = in order; всё в порядке = everything is fine

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'check, inspection, test' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An inspection is underway at the bank.

examples.text: Эксперты уже начали проверку состояния старой стены.
examples.trans: Experts have already begun checking the condition of the old wall.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.trans: You think he is testing us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'веряющий'). Common masculine noun meaning 'inspector' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проверяющий живёт здесь как обычный гость.
examples.trans: The inspector stays here like an ordinary guest.

examples.text: Она сказала, что этот господин — проверяющий.
examples.trans: She said that this gentleman was the inspector.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'снуться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wake up'.

examples.trans: Vika, are you awake already today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сыпаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wake up', paired with 'проснуться'.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Дорожная служба = road service. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лужба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лужба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'service, department' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Дорожная служба обещала закатать её десять лет назад.
examples.trans: The road service promised to pave it over ten years ago.
Right now we need to call social services.

meanings.en: way, method, means of doing something
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пособ'). Common masculine noun meaning 'way, method, means' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.
examples.trans: The strong man looks for a way, and the weak man looks for an excuse.

examples.text: Мы нашли простой способ решить задачу.
examples.trans: We found a simple way to solve the problem.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('secret, hidden').

examples.text: Тогда я сама выберу другое тайное место.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Утром = in the morning. Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
